newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee gains in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee gains in volatile trade.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee moved up against the dollar in brisk Thursday morning trade that was driven by speculators, dealers said.
At 0600 GMT the rupee was at 58.46 to the dollar, after opening at 58.55 and moving to 58.35, they said.
"The rupee rose to 58.35 on dollar sell-offs after the Central Bank announced its trading range," said a dealer at American Express Bank.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by six local cents, fixing buying and selling rates at 58.1501 and 59.3249.
Dealers said the Central Bank's action, which was prompted by the greenback's easing overseas, also enhanced the belief that depreciation of the rupee may have ended.

"Banks, which began selling the dollar aggressively two days ago in the belief that short-term depreciation targets have been met, sold even more after today's Central Bank action," said the American Express dealer.

Overnight call money rates, meanwhile were also volatile due to a lack of sellers, dealers said. "Call rates were at 16 percent, after opening at 11 and rising to 20 due to a lack of selling," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
